name: Pixel Art
description: Artwork drawn on a strict integer grid with hard edges, deliberate colour clusters and no anti-aliasing. Every pixel is a decision; form comes from clusters, dithering and readable silhouettes.
visual_characteristics: single square grid (e.g. 16x16, 32x32, 64x64); every shape is an integer-aligned block
limited palette (typically 8-24 colours) organised in hue-shifted ramps
1-pixel dark outline or selective outlining; clean staircase lines (2:1 or 1:1 slopes)
clusters instead of noise; dithering only where it adds form

palette.guidance: Hue-shifted ramps of 3-5 colours per material: shadows shift toward cool/purple, highlights toward warm/yellow. Keep a shared dark outline colour that is NOT pure black. 8-24 colours total.

geometry: Rectangles on integer coordinates only. Diagonals as clean 1:1 or 2:1 staircases; circles as classic pixel-circle arrangements. No curves, no sub-pixel offsets, no rotation except multiples of 90 degrees.
stroke: No SVG strokes. Outlines are pixels (cells) of an outline colour. Selective outlining: darker tone of the fill on the lit side.
texture: Ordered (Bayer 2x2/4x4) or hand-placed dithering for gradients and material texture, kept on the grid.
composition: Design at the target grid size first (e.g. 32x32), strong silhouette, 1-2 px padding. Even pixel size everywhere (no mixed-resolution pixels).
typography: Bitmap-style letters built from the same grid (5x7 or 3x5 cells). Do not use <text> with smooth fonts.
lighting_depth: Two-to-three-step cel shading with a fixed light direction (top-left). Ground shadow as a dithered or flat ellipse of cells.
svg_techniques: author sprites as ASCII with scripts/pixel_grid.py -> one merged <path> per colour, integer coordinates
viewBox equals the grid size (e.g. 0 0 32 32) so it scales by integer factors

name: Retro 8-bit
description: The NES / Game Boy / C64 era: tiny grids, tight colour budgets per sprite, chunky silhouettes and a fixed hardware-style palette.
visual_characteristics: grid 16x16 or 32x32 sprites; scenes on 8x8 tiles up to 256x240 logical resolution
max 3 colours + transparent per sprite; <= 16 colours in the whole scene
flat cel shading, almost no dithering; bold 1px outlines
HUD-like framing: score bars, borders and blocky lettering

palette.guidance: Pick ONE hardware palette and stay inside it: NES-like (saturated reds, blues, greens, olive, cream) or Game Boy 4-green ramp or C64 muted tones. Never invent gradient colours.

geometry: 8x8 tile logic: shapes snap to multiples of a base cell. Chunky, symmetrical sprites; very simple readable silhouettes; hard-coded tile repetition for backgrounds (brick, grass, water).
stroke: Pixel outlines only. 1-cell outline in the darkest palette colour.
texture: None or two-tone checker tiles (brick/water) repeated on the tile grid.
composition: Side-view or top-down with flat horizontal ground band; sprite large relative to the screen; sky as a flat colour or two-tone band; HUD strip at top.
typography: 8x8 bitmap font drawn from cells (uppercase, no anti-aliasing), e.g. 'SCORE 000100'.
lighting_depth: No lighting model; depth via parallax bands (2-3 flat layers) and overlap.
svg_techniques: everything from pixel_grid.py paths; scene tiles built with <pattern> of an integer-sized tile
root shape-rendering="crispEdges"; viewBox equal to logical resolution (e.g. 0 0 128 112)
keep the palette in one comment and reuse only those hexes

name: Retro 16-bit
description: The SNES / Mega Drive era: richer palettes, multi-step shading, dithered skies, detailed sprites on 32-64px grids and layered parallax backgrounds.
visual_characteristics: sprites 32x32 to 64x64 with 3-5 step shading ramps and selective outlining
palettes of 16-32 colours per scene with carefully hue-shifted ramps
dithered gradients for skies, glows and shadows
layered parallax backgrounds (far mountains, mid trees, near foreground)

palette.guidance: Ramp-based: each material has 4-5 steps with hue shift (cool shadows, warm highlights). Scene is unified by an atmospheric tint on distant layers. 16-32 colours total.

geometry: Integer cells, staircase curves (anti-aliased-looking edges are made with intermediate-tone pixels only if the tone is a real palette colour), pixel circles, chunky proportions but more anatomy than 8-bit.
stroke: Pixel outlines, coloured (selective) rather than black; interior lines in darker fill tone.
texture: Bayer/hand dithering for skies, water and stone; specular pixel highlights on metal and eyes.
composition: Cinematic side-on or 3/4 top-down; foreground / mid / background parallax planes; strong horizon; focal character in the lower third with glow behind.
typography: Pixel font with 1px drop shadow, 8x8 or 8x12; menu frames with double borders and corner ornaments.
lighting_depth: Single light direction plus rim light; atmospheric perspective by recolouring far layers toward the sky colour; glow through concentric hard-edged rings.
svg_techniques: pixel_grid.py for sprites; backgrounds as one <path> per colour per layer
dither as <pattern> tiles of 2x2 or 4x4 integer size
crispEdges on root; keep layers as <g id="far"> <g id="mid"> <g id="near">
emulate glow with stepped concentric pixel rings, never blur
avoid: curves and circles as SVG primitives
